result.markdown:
# High Latency Incident on Site S-SFX-008

- **Classification:** incident
- **Root cause:** capacity at `S-SFX-008`
- **Confidence:** high (Direct telemetry anomalies and warning alarms observed on S-SFX-008 coinciding with the latency spike, while sibling sites remained unaffected.)
- **Impact:** 2026-09-12 17:15 to 2026-09-12 18:45
- **Cause time:** 2026-09-12 17:15
- **Affected:** S-SFX-008

## Summary

Traffic and data volume surge caused high PRB utilization, dropping RRC success, and elevated latency on site S-SFX-008.

Elevated latency, increased traffic, and higher drop rates occurred on site S-SFX-008 for 1.5 hours.

## Timeline

- 2026-09-12 16:02: Parameter tuning change applied to S-SFX-008. [CHG-2026-0034]
- 2026-09-12 17:15: Latency, traffic and drop rate spike began on S-SFX-008. [ALR-0013, ANM-000177]
- 2026-09-12 17:25: High PRB utilization warning alarm raised on S-SFX-008. [ALM-000241]
- 2026-09-12 18:45: Anomaly ALR-0013 ended on S-SFX-008. [ALR-0013]
- 2026-09-12 18:56: High PRB warning alarm cleared on S-SFX-008. [ALM-000241]

## Evidence

- S-SFX-008 experienced a severe downlink volume spike from a baseline of 24943 to 109773. [ANM-000175]
- Latency on S-SFX-008 increased from a baseline of 21.6 ms to 89.1 ms. [ANM-000177]
- Drop rate on S-SFX-008 spiked from 0.6 percent to 2.73 percent. [ANM-000176]
- Sibling sites S-SFX-005 and S-SFX-010 remained stable during the incident window. [T6]
- No external events occurred in region SFX between 2026-09-12 10:00 and 2026-09-12 20:00. [T3]
- No maintenance window was scheduled on S-SFX-008 and its parents during the incident window. [T7]

## Hypotheses

1. **capacity** at S-SFX-008: confirmed. Traffic surge directly caused high PRB utilization and latency spikes on S-SFX-008. [ALR-0013, ANM-000175, ALM-000241]
2. **bad_change** at S-SFX-008: rejected. Parameter changes were applied to S-SFX-005 and S-SFX-010 as well, but only S-SFX-008 experienced the degradation. [CHG-2026-0034, CHG-2026-0035, CHG-2026-0036, T6]

## Ruled out

- CHG-2026-0034: Parameter changes were also deployed on sibling sites S-SFX-005 and S-SFX-010 which experienced no latency or drop rate issues.
- CHG-2026-0035: Sibling site S-SFX-010 remained stable after receiving this parameter tuning change.
- CHG-2026-0036: Sibling site S-SFX-005 remained stable after receiving this parameter tuning change.

## Recommended actions

- Monitor traffic trends on S-SFX-008 to determine if capacity expansion is required.
- Review scheduler weight tuning settings to ensure they did not contribute to traffic concentration.

## Sources

- `CHG-2026-0034`: parameter_tuning on S-SFX-008 at 2026-09-12 16:02: Scheduler weight tuning on S-SFX-008
- `ALR-0013`: ended alert from 2026-09-12 17:15: 1 site(s) (S-SFX-008); core CORE-UPF-02; region-level SFX; metrics: active_users, dl_volume_mb, drop_rate_pct, latency_ms, prb_util_...

confounders.why: Harmless parameter_tuning on S-SFX-008 68 min before the congestion; the cause is a demand surge and neighbours with the same tuning were unaffected.

truth.notes: trap=change_on_root_node; Demand surge saturated the radio resources of S-SFX-008; there was no external event. Trap: a scheduler tuning on S-SFX-008 itself ran 68 min before the congestion, so a hasty investigator blames the change. Settled by: (1) the number of active users roughly doubled, which a scheduler setting cannot do; (2) the same tuning under the same ticket went onto S-SFX-005, S-SFX-010 and their load and PRB stayed normal; (3) the KPIs were normal between the change and the onset.
